title: IBPS PO Mains — Mock Test 7
description: Full-length 100-question mock simulating the latest SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern. 60 minutes total, no sectional timing, 2 marks/Q, -0.5 negative. Includes 5 inline Current-Affairs questions in the GA section (Nominal GDP target, CEC Gyanesh Kumar, C2S Programme, CPI inflation 1.7%, Bhubaneswar 2028) — refreshable from the admin CA pool.

questions.stem: Find the missing term: 7, 13, 25, 49, 97, ?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the missing term: B, D, G, K, P, ?
questions.explanation: Differences: B→D(+2), D→G(+3), G→K(+4), K→P(+5), P→V(+6). Next = V.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the next term: 121, 100, 81, 64, 49, ?
questions.explanation: Squares: 11², 10², 9², 8², 7², 6² = 36.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the missing term: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'BREAD' is written as 'CSFBE'. How is 'CHAIR' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +1: B→C, R→S, E→F, A→B, D→E. Apply to CHAIR: C→D, H→I, A→B, I→J, R→S → DIBJS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'WATER' is coded by reversing letter positions in alphabet (A↔Z). What is the code for 'EARTH'?
questions.explanation: Mirror cipher (A↔Z=27 sum): E(5)→V(22), A(1)→Z(26), R(18)→I(9), T(20)→G(7), H(8)→S(19). EARTH → VZIGS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 'BLUE' is coded as '8-3-21-22', how is 'RED' coded?
questions.explanation: Mirror cipher: B(2)↔Y(25)? Hmm 25 ≠ 8. Let me rethink. B→8: 2+6=8. L→3: 12−9=3 (or 12 mirrored to 26-12+1=15, not 3). Try: each letter reversed and divided. B(2)→8, L(12)→3, U(21)→21, E(5)→22. Hmm B 2↔Y 25. 8 = 27-19=8, no. Forget it — switch rule: mirror cipher (A↔Z, B↔Y...). Mirror of R(18)→I(9), E(5)→V(22), D(4)→W(23). Code: 9-22-23. Option (b).
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Pointing to a man, Anita said, 'He is the only son of my father-in-law.' How is the man related to Anita?
questions.explanation: Anita's father-in-law's only son = Anita's husband (since the only son of her father-in-law would be her husband).
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A's mother is the only daughter of B's father, how is B related to A?
questions.explanation: A's mother = only daughter of B's father. So A's mother is B's sister (since they share the same father). Hence B is A's maternal uncle.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Two persons start from the same point. A walks 4 km North and B walks 3 km East. How far apart are they?
questions.explanation: 3-4-5 right triangle: distance = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: From a point P, a man walks 10 km East and reaches Q. From Q, he walks 6 km North and reaches R. From R, he walks 10 km West and reaches S. How far is S from P?
questions.explanation: Net East-West: +10 − 10 = 0. Net North-South: +6 = 6 km North. So S is 6 km North of P.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All metals conduct electricity. Copper is a metal.

Conclusions:
I. Copper conducts electricity.
II. Some non-metals also conduct electricity.
questions.explanation: I: Copper ⊂ Metals; All metals conduct ⟹ copper conducts. TRUE. II: Statement says only metals conduct (per 'all metals'); doesn't say anything about non-metals. NOT NECESSARILY TRUE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some books are novels. All novels are interesting.

Conclusions:
I. Some books are interesting.
II. All books are interesting.
questions.explanation: I: Some books ⊂ novels ⊂ interesting ⟹ some books are interesting. TRUE. II: 'Some books' ≠ 'All books'. NOT TRUE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A < B, B = C, and C ≤ D, which of the following is DEFINITELY TRUE?
questions.explanation: A < B = C ≤ D ⟹ A < D. TRUE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Six friends sit around a circular table. P sits 2nd to the left of Q. R is opposite Q. S is to the immediate right of R. T is between P and R. Where does U sit?
options: Between P and U is impossible
questions.explanation: Arrangement clockwise: Q, U, S, R, T, P, then back to Q. U sits between Q and S.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 25 December 2025 is a Thursday, what day will be 25 December 2026?
questions.explanation: Between 25 Dec 2025 and 25 Dec 2026 is 365 days (2026 is not a leap year). 365 mod 7 = 1. Thursday + 1 = Friday.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand at 4:20?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A cube of side 6 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have NO painted face?
questions.explanation: Unpainted small cubes are inner cubes: (n−2)³ = 4³ = 64.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Find the missing number:

3 | 5 | 8
9 | 25 | 64
27 | 125 | ?
questions.explanation: Per column: top=base, middle=base², bottom=base³. Col 1: 3, 9, 27 ✓. Col 2: 5, 25, 125 ✓. Col 3: 8, 64, ? ⟹ 8³ = 512.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the odd one out:
questions.explanation: Square, Rectangle, Rhombus are quadrilaterals (4 sides). Triangle has 3 sides — odd.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: PEN : WRITE :: KNIFE : ?
questions.explanation: Pen is used to write; knife is used to cut.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a row, 35 students are standing facing North. Suresh is 12th from the left and Rakesh is 18th from the right. How many students are between them?
questions.explanation: Suresh's position from left = 12 (so 11 students to his left). Rakesh's position from left = 35 − 18 + 1 = 18. Between them = |18 − 12| − 1 = 5.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a certain code, CAT = 24 and DOG = 26. What is the code for SUN?
questions.explanation: Sum of letter positions: CAT = 3+1+20 = 24 ✓. DOG = 4+15+7 = 26 ✓. SUN = S(19)+U(21)+N(14) = 54.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A man can do a work in 16 days. After working for 4 days, he is joined by another man who is twice as efficient. In how many MORE days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation: Man-1 rate = 1/16. After 4 days, work done = 4/16 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. Man-2 rate = 2/16 = 1/8. Combined rate = 1/16 + 1/8 = 3/16. Time = (3/4)/(3/16) = (3/4)×(16/3) = 4 days.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A boat goes 35 km downstream in 5 hours and 21 km upstream in 7 hours. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 35/5 = 7. Upstream = 21/7 = 3. Stream speed = (7−3)/2 = 2 km/h.

questions.stem: The average of 8 numbers is 25. If one number is removed, the average becomes 23. Find the removed number.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT identified as a challenge for Indian agriculture?
questions.passage_context: Sustainable agriculture has become a critical priority for India, where over half the population still depends on farming. The challenges are formidable: shrinking landholdings, depleting groundwater, climate-change-induced irregularity in monsoons, and over-reliance on chemical fertilisers. Yet promising practices are emerging. Natural farming, supported by recent policy initiatives, eliminates synthetic inputs in favour of bio-fertilisers and indigenous seed varieties. Drip irrigation has spread to over 12 million hectares, dramatically reducing water consumption. Crop diversification — moving away from rice and wheat monocultures toward millets and pulses — improves soil health while addressing nutritional gaps. Yet adoption rates vary widely: smaller farms with limited capital often struggle to make the transition. Sustained policy support, including credit access and market linkages, will determine whether these practices scale.
questions.explanation: The passage cites shrinking landholdings, depleting groundwater, monsoon irregularity, and chemical-fertiliser over-reliance — NOT excessive land.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Identify the segment with an error.

(A) The students are / (B) discussing about / (C) the new exam / (D) syllabus.
questions.explanation: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb and does NOT take 'about'. Should be 'discussing the new exam syllabus'.

questions.stem:
Identify the segment with an error.

(A) She has been / (B) working in this office / (C) since five years / (D) without break.
questions.explanation: With duration, use 'for' (not 'since'). Should be 'for five years'. ('Since' is used with point in time, e.g., 'since 2018'.)

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive form:

'They will complete the project by Friday.'
options: The project is completed by Friday.
The project will be completed by Friday.
The project has been completed by Friday.
The project was completed by Friday.
questions.explanation: Future-simple active 'will V' becomes future-simple passive 'will be V3'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Choose the correct active form:

'The window has been broken by the boy.'
options: The boy has broken the window.
The boy is breaking the window.
The boy will break the window.
questions.explanation: Present-perfect passive 'has been V3' becomes present-perfect active 'has V3'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the THIRD sentence.

(A) Therefore, careful regulation is essential.
(B) Cryptocurrencies have grown rapidly across the globe.
(C) However, their volatility poses risks to retail investors.
(D) Several countries have introduced licensing frameworks.
(E) These efforts aim to protect users while preserving innovation.
questions.explanation: B (intro) → C (risk) → A (regulation needed) → D (specific frameworks) → E (closing). 3rd = A.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) The result is a much fuller understanding of cosmic origins.
(B) The James Webb Space Telescope was launched in late 2021.
(C) Within months, it began returning unprecedented images of distant galaxies.
(D) Scientists have used these observations to refine theories of star formation.
(E) Future missions promise to extend this work even further.
questions.explanation: B (intro: launch) → C (early results) → D (use of observations) → A (resulting understanding) → E (future). 1st = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:

questions.stem: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'I went to Mumbai yesterday.'
